$comment: Single source of truth for a reverse-engineering dossier (see SKILL.md, Verification spine, and references/verification.md). validate_dossier.py reads this file directly and interprets it -- there is no second copy of these rules to keep in sync. A dossier is ONE object per target. Every claim carries a kind that fixes its epistemic weight: ground_truth (what a tool literally shows -- must cite tool+locator+literal), hypothesis (believed meaning -- must cite the basis it rests on), behavioural (what the target DOES at runtime -- confirmed only with dynamic/sandbox evidence, otherwise a labelled guess). Schema subset interpreted by the validator: type (object|array|string|integer|boolean), properties, required, additionalProperties:false, enum, const, items, minItems, oneOf. Constraints the subset cannot express (unique ids, supports-references, confirmed-needs-dynamic-evidence) are applied as a labelled semantic layer after schema validation.

dossier_schema.description: One dossier per target: the mechanism asked about, every statement split into ground truth, hypothesis, and behaviour.

target.description: What was analysed: a URL, a file path, or a content hash. Be specific and resolvable.

tier.description: Which tier of the skill produced this dossier.

question.description: The mechanism asked about, in one sentence. e.g. 'How does the scroll drive the reel animation?'

lawful_basis.description: Why this analysis is permitted. The gate: only lawful purposes are representable here.

purpose.description: interoperability = EU Software Directive 2009/24/EC art.6 conditions; security_research = finding/understanding vulnerabilities; format_understanding = reading an undocumented file/wire format; own_work = a target you own or are contracted on; education = learning how a technique works.

note.description: One sentence naming the concrete basis (which client, which program, which format).

analyst_date.description: ISO date the analysis was performed (YYYY-MM-DD).

claims.description: Every statement in the dossier, each tagged by kind. A claim with no evidence of the kind its tag demands is a schema failure.

oneOf.description: Ground truth: what a tool literally output. Not interpreted. Cite the tool, where it came from, and the literal bytes/text.

id.description: Unique within the dossier. Referenced by hypotheses.

statement.description: The literal fact, stated flatly. No 'this means'.

tool.description: What produced it: fingerprint.py, capture_net.py, objdump, radare2, the response headers, etc.

locator.description: Where exactly: a response header name, a request URL, a file offset, an instruction address, a line in a beautified file.

literal.description: The exact string/bytes the tool showed. Quote it; do not paraphrase.

oneOf.description: Hypothesis: what the ground truth is believed to MEAN. Always provisional. Must name the basis it rests on.

statement.description: The interpretation. Written so it could be proven wrong.

basis.description: Why this reading is plausible: the reasoning from the ground truth to the meaning.

supports.description: ids of the ground_truth (or behavioural) claims this rests on. Each must exist in the dossier (enforced by the validator).

oneOf.description: Behavioural: a claim about what the target DOES at runtime (phones home, writes a file, loads this on scroll). Static reading alone can never confirm one. status 'confirmed' REQUIRES dynamic/sandbox evidence (enforced by the validator); otherwise it stays 'unconfirmed' -- a labelled guess.

status.description: confirmed = observed in a dynamic/sandbox run (evidence required). unconfirmed = suspected from static reading only (a labelled guess).

evidence.description: Required when status is 'confirmed'. The method must be a dynamic observation; a behavioural fact cannot be confirmed on static evidence.

method.description: How it was observed running: dynamic trace, sandbox execution, or live runtime capture (e.g. capture_net.py).

locator.description: Where in the run: a captured request, a syscall, a traced address at a timestamp.

literal.description: The exact observed artifact: the request line, the syscall, the written path.
